assessments.reasoning: The commit-pinned Jove LICENSE is the complete Jonathan Payne copyright and permission notice, including the condition about retaining the notice. Its capture hash matches the claim's publisher revision.
Decoded licenseText under the exact lowercase identifier jove is byte-identical to the entire publisher notice.
The pinned jove.txt independently matches the publisher LICENSE byte for byte and yields the same 43 tokens.
The SPDX license-list-data annotated v3.29.0 tag targets commit 31ba1a50e5397e00a304dbadc76531740e89ee48. The exact json/details/jove.json and text/jove.txt URLs both use that repository and commit.

challenge.method: Compared the complete captured Jove LICENSE with decoded JSON licenseText and the standalone text as ordered, case-folded alphanumeric tokens and as UTF-8 bytes. Changed the terminal copyright year as a same-count control. Checked the annotated tag against the two exact SPDX URLs and inspected the publisher pin and SPDX cross-reference.
challenge.results: The full publisher notice and both SPDX texts contain 43 tokens and are byte-identical, including punctuation, spacing, and the final newline. The 1986–2001 control still has 43 tokens and fails both comparisons. The fixed publisher URL names a commit, while the cross-reference names 4_17. Their ref-to-commit relationship is unverified.

limitations: The captured LICENSE establishes the notice at the cited commit. Applicability across Jove releases and resolution of the 4_17 cross-reference remain unverified.
Legal equivalence, rights for other works, text reuse, installation, and Index lifecycle are outside scope.
The release tag is unsigned. The supplied SCES commit and bundle digest were not independently verified from bundle bytes.
reasoning: The exact pinned identifier and both SPDX bodies support the claimed correspondence for the complete captured notice. Recomputed UTF-8 lengths, digests, and body ranges agree with the envelopes.
